messages.author: 817de18ddde0ac9e
messages.subject: Error message in all GGIR scripts, step count & sedentary time
parts:
Hello everyone

I am a student at the University of Berne and we are doing the active school project with the geneactive watches. For this severeal struggles got up:

1) I read several GGIR documents and ran the script multiple times. In the beginning it worked fine, but suddenly this error message came up: Error in if TRUE :
argument is of length zero
Unfortunately I have no idea what's going on, because I haven't changed anything in the script. This message also comes up when I run other (simpler) scripts. Can someone help me?

2) Furthermore, I read through many this conversations but I could not find any codes to compute the step counts. Is there a way besides the one with Verisense? Because I can't find any script or downloads from verisense to compute it.

3) In the end, I should have the sedentary time. How can I do it? I read something about defining the thresholds, but I could not implement it. Could you help me here as well?


Thank you in advance,
Elena

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: Error message in all GGIR scripts, step count & sedentary time
parts:
Hi Elena,

1) No-one will be able to help unless you include more information, including at least a copy of the script you are trying to run - see the instructions about what should be included in a post at the top of the google group.

2) There is not another step detection algorithm which works with GGIR that I am aware of other than Verisense. The scripts and instructions for Verisense can be found here: https://github.com/ShimmerEngineering/Verisense-Toolbox/tree/master/Verisense_step_algorithm

3) You will be looking for inactivity time, not sedentary time in the outputs (e.g. dur_day_IN_xxx) but without the script that you ran I can't help more than that other than read section 4.3 here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html

thanks,
Ben

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Error message in all GGIR scripts, step count & sedentary time
parts: For 3) I know that there is inactivity time, but I really would like to have the sedentary time.

As explained in other recent threads sedentary behaviour measurement is a myth. Research tools typically either estimate time spent with thigh horizontal which could be sitting or lying or time spent below an acceleration threshold.

In GGIR we call it inactivity because we only look at the acceleration threshold, this to avoid the misleading impression that we are attempting to detect when people have their thigh horizontal. Nonetheless, most publications that have used GGIR refer to these estimates as sedentary behaviour because of peer-pressure in the research community to stick to popular terminology. However, in GGIR we try to avoid using the term sedentary behaviour.

So, if you want to extract the thing that others who have used wrist-accelerometry call sedentary behaviour then you will have to use the inactivity estimates.

I see you have a lot of question. You may want to consider signing up to our GGIR training course where we provide an overview of all there is to know about GGIR: https://www.accelting.com/ggir-training/

Best wishes,

Vincent
